questions.question: Is the problem recurring and painful enough to pay to solve?
questions.answer: Coaches regularly pay recurring subscriptions for platforms like Trainerize ($10–$135/mo), but complain about rising costs as client count scales ($77/mo for 30 clients) and unexpected add-on costs.
questions.notes: Evidence confirms high spending on SaaS platforms, but specific churn/quitting due solely to software pain is inferred.

questions.question: What exactly have people already tried, and why did it fall short?
questions.answer: Trainers use Trainerize, TrueCoach, My PT Hub, and Notion/Sheets templates. Dedicated SaaS falls short due to steep pricing scaling with client count and extra monthly add-on fees ($4.99–$14.99/mo per feature).
questions.notes: Direct user posts and reviews highlight cost frustrations with per-client tier scaling.

questions.question: Is a digital product the right form, or is this a service/free-info problem?
questions.answer: A digital product (such as a one-time purchase spreadsheet or Notion template) is an appropriate fit, as trainers seek tools to organize client programs without recurring seat/client subscription costs.
questions.notes: Spreadsheet and Notion template alternatives exist to replace monthly per-seat SaaS costs.

questions.question: What is the single most useful asset we could ship?
questions.answer: A reusable Google Sheets/Excel workout program template and client tracking dashboard with no monthly per-client pricing.
questions.notes: Templates directly solve the program reuse and scale pain without recurring SaaS fees.

questions.question: What price will the audience tolerate, and on what evidence?
questions.answer: For digital templates, trainers tolerate a one-time price of $1.99 to $19.99 (or up to ~$40 for comprehensive Notion/Sheets systems). For entry-level SaaS, budget solo-coaches tolerate $10–$25/mo.
questions.notes: Observed market prices for spreadsheet template alternatives range from $1.99-$19.99, while basic SaaS starts around $10-$25/mo.
